   b = reshape([ 5.0_dp, 6.0_dp ], shape(b))               ! single column
   c = 0.0_dp                                            ! will be filled

   !------------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Core algorithm – faithful recreation of the original loops for the
   ! double‑precision path (IPREC = 2).
   !------------------------------------------------------------------
   do i = 1, ncola
      !--- Unpack column i of A into the first half of WORK ----------------
      call unpack_column(a, i, work(1:nrowa))

      !--- Unpack column of B (or reuse the single column) -----------------
      if (ncolb = 1) then
         if (i == 1) then
            call unpack_column(b, 1, work(nrowa+1:2*nrowa))
         else
            ! Re‑use the already‑unpacked column – do nothing.
         end if
      else
         call unpack_column(b, i, work(nrowa+1:2*nrowa))
      end if

      !--- Compute element‑wise product scaled by GG -----------------------
      do j = 1, nrowa
         work(j) = gg * work(j) * work(nrowa + j)
      end do

      !--- Pack the result back into column i of C ------------------------
      call pack_column(c, i, work(1:nrowa))
   end do

   do i = 1, nrowa

                     bnd,mb,time,meqn)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: mx, my, mb, dir, meqn
    integer, intent(in) :: lb(2), ub(2), lbbnd(2), ubbnd(2), shapebnd(2)
    real(dp), intent(inout) :: u(meqn,mx,my)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: xc(2), dx(2), bnd(mb,2,2), time

    integer :: i, j, m, imin, imax, jmin, jmax, jsym, isym
    integer :: stride, ibnd
    integer, parameter :: isx(4) = (/1, -1, 1, 1/)
    integer, parameter :: isy(4) = (/1,  1,-1, 1/)

    ! For this demonstration we simply treat the boundary as inflow/outflow
    ibnd = 1

    stride = (ub(1) - lb(1)) / (mx - 1)

    imin = getindx( max(real(lbbnd(1),dp), real(lb(1),dp)), lb(1), stride )
    imax = getindx( min(real(ubbnd(1),dp), real(ub(1),dp)), lb(1), stride )
    jmin = getindx( max(real(lbbnd(2),dp), real(lb(2),dp)), lb(2), stride )
    jmax = getindx( min(real(ubbnd(2),dp), real(ub(2),dp)), lb(2), stride )

    if (imax > mx .or. jmax > my .or. imin < 1 .or. jmin < 1) then
       print *, 'INDEX ERROR in physbd'
       return
    end if

    select case (dir)
    case (0)   ! Left side – inflow/outflow
       do i = imax, imin, -1
          if ( xc(1) + (i-0.5_dp)*dx(1) < bnd(1,1,1) ) then
             do j = jmin, jmax
                do m = 1, meqn
                   u(m,i,j) = u(m,i+1,j)
                end do
             end do
          end if
       end do

    case (1)   ! Right side – inflow/outflow or reflection
       do i = imin, imax
          if ( xc(1) + (i-0.5_dp)*dx(1) > bnd(1,2,1) ) then
             if (ibnd == 1) then
                do j = jmin, jmax
                   do m = 1, meqn
                      u(m,i,j) = u(m,i-1,j)
                   end do
                end do
             else
                isym = 2*imin - 1 - i
                do j = jmin, jmax
                   do m = 1, meqn
                      u(m,i,j) = u(m,isym,j) * isx(m)
                   end do
                end do
             end if
          end if
       end do

    case (2)   ! Bottom side – reflection
       do j = jmax, jmin, -1
          if ( xc(2) + (j-0.5_dp)*dx(2) < bnd(1,1,2) ) then
             jsym = 2*jmax + 1 - j
             do i = imin, imax
                do m = 1, meqn
                   u(m,i,j) = u(m,i,jsym) * isy(m)
                end do
             end do
          end if
       end do

    case (3)   ! Top side – reflection
       do j = jmin, jmax
          if ( xc(2) + (j-0.5_dp)*dx(2) > bnd(1,2,2) ) then
             jsym = 2*jmin - 1 - j
             do i = imin, imax
                do m = 1, meqn
                   u(m,i,j) = u(m,i,jsym) * isy(m)
                end do
             end do
          end if
       end do

    case default
       print *, 'Invalid dir value in physbd: ', dir
    end select

  end subroutine physbd

   !================================================================
   !  DLARFG – generate elementary reflector (Householder vector)
   !================================================================
   subroutine dlarfg(n, alpha, x, incx, tau)
      implicit none
      integer, intent(in) :: n, incx
      real(wp), intent(inout) :: alpha
      real(wp), intent(inout) :: x(*)
      real(wp), intent(out) :: tau

      real(wp) :: xnorm, beta, safemin, rsafmn
      integer :: i, ix, iter

      if (n <= 1) then
         tau = 0.0_wp
         return
      end if

      ! Compute the Euclidean norm of the vector x[1:n-1]
      xnorm = 0.0_wp
      ix = 1
      do i = 2, n
         xnorm = xnorm + x(ix)**2
         ix = ix + incx
      end do
      xnorm = sqrt(xnorm)

      if (xnorm == 0.0_wp .and. alpha >= 0.0_wp) then
         tau = 0.0_wp
         return
      end if

      beta = -sign(sqrt(alpha*alpha + xnorm*xnorm), alpha)
      safemin = tiny(1.0_wp)
      rsafmn = 1.0_wp / safemin
      if (abs(beta) < safemin) then
         ! Scale the vector to avoid underflow
         do iter = 1, 1000   ! just a safety guard – in practice never reached
            ix = 1
            do i = 2, n
               x(ix) = x(ix) * rsafmn
               ix = ix + incx
            end do
            alpha = alpha * rsafmn
            beta = beta * rsafmn
            if (abs(beta) >= safemin) exit
         end do
      end if

      tau = (beta - alpha) / beta
      ix = 1
      do i = 2, n
         x(ix) = x(ix) / (alpha - beta)
         ix = ix + incx
      end do
      alpha = beta
   end subroutine dlarfg

   !================================================================
   !  DLARF – apply elementary reflector H = I - tau*v*v^T
   !================================================================
   subroutine dlarf(side, m, n, v, incv, tau, c, ldc, work)
      implicit none
      character(len=*), intent(in) :: side
      integer, intent(in) :: m, n, incv, ldc
      real(wp), intent(in) :: v(*)
      real(wp), intent(in) :: tau
      real(wp), intent(inout) :: c(ldc, *)
      real(wp), intent(out) :: work(*)

      integer :: i, j
      real(wp) :: wtmp

      if (tau == 0.0_wp) return

      if (side == 'Left' .or. side == 'LEFT' .or. side == 'left') then
         ! w = tau * v^T * C   (size n)
         do j = 1, n
            wtmp = 0.0_wp
            i = 1
            do while (i <= m)
               wtmp = wtmp + v(i) * c(i,j)
               i = i + incv
            end do
            work(j) = tau * wtmp
         end do
         ! C = C - v * w^T
         i = 1
         do while (i <= m)
            do j = 1, n
               c(i,j) = c(i,j) - v(i) * work(j)
            end do
            i = i + incv
         end do
      else
         ! side == 'Right'
         ! w = tau * C * v   (size m)
         do i = 1, m
            wtmp = 0.0_wp
            j = 1
            do while (j <= n)
               wtmp = wtmp + c(i,j) * v(j)
               j = j + incv
            end do
            work(i) = tau * wtmp
         end do
         ! C = C - w * v^T
         i = 1
         do while (i <= m)
            do j = 1, n
               c(i,j) = c(i,j) - work(i) * v(j)
            end do
            i = i + 1
         end do
      end if

   end subroutine dlarf

      implicit none

  !============================================================
  subroutine dgbsl(abd, lda, n, ml, mu, ipvt, b, job)

contains

  !============================================================
  ! DGBSL – solves a banded system using LU factors from DGBFA/DGBCO.
  ! This is a faithful translation of the original routine with
  ! modern syntax and explicit typing.  No nested internal procedures
  ! are used (Fortran does not permit a CONTAINS statement inside an
  ! internal subprogram), so the forward/back‑substitution code is
  ! written inline.
  !============================================================
  subroutine dgbsl(abd, lda, n, ml, mu, ipvt, b, job)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in)    :: lda, n, ml, mu, ipvt(*), job
    real(dp), intent(in)   :: abd(lda, *)
    real(dp), intent(inout):: b(*)

    integer :: k, kb, l, la, lb, lm, m_local, nm1
    real(dp) :: t

    m_local = mu + ml + 1
    nm1     = n - 1

    if (job /= 0) then
       !-------------------------------
       ! Solve trans(A) * x = b
       !-------------------------------

       !--- solve trans(U) * y = b
       do k = 1, n
          lm = min(k, m_local) - 1
          la = m_local - lm
          lb = k - lm
          t = ddot(lm, abd(la, k), 1, b(lb), 1)
          b(k) = (b(k) - t) / abd(m_local, k)
       end do

       !--- solve trans(L) * x = y
       if (ml /= 0 .and. nm1 >= 1) then
          do kb = 1, nm1
             k = n - kb
             lm = min(ml, n - k)
             b(k) = b(k) + ddot(lm, abd(m_local+1, k), 1, b(k+1), 1)
             l = ipvt(k)
             if (l /= k) then
                t   = b(l)
                b(l)= b(k)
                b(k)= t
             end if
          end do
       end if

    else
       !-------------------------------
       ! Solve A * x = b
       !-------------------------------

       !--- forward substitution: solve L*y = b
       if (ml /= 0 .and. nm1 >= 1) then
          do k = 1, nm1
             lm = min(ml, n - k)
             l  = ipvt(k)
             t  = b(l)
             if (l /= k) then
                b(l) = b(k)
                b(k) = t
             end if
             call daxpy(lm, t, abd(m_local+1, k), 1, b(k+1), 1)
          end do
       end if

       !--- back substitution: solve U*x = y
       do kb = 1, n
          k  = n + 1 - kb
          b(k) = b(k) / abd(m_local, k)
          lm = min(k, m_local) - 1
          la = m_local - lm
          lb = k - lm
          t = -b(k)
          call daxpy(lm, t, abd(la, k), 1, b(lb), 1)
       end do

    end if

  end subroutine dgbsl

  !============================================================
  ! DAXPY – y := a*x + y   (simple BLAS level‑1 routine)
  !============================================================
  subroutine daxpy(n, a, x, incx, y, incy)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in)           :: n, incx, incy
    real(dp), intent(in)          :: a, x(*)
    real(dp), intent(inout)       :: y(*)
    integer                       :: i, ix, iy
    if (n <= 0) return
    ix = 1
    iy = 1
    do i = 1, n
       y(iy) = y(iy) + a * x(ix)
       ix = ix + incx
       iy = iy + incy
    end do
  end subroutine daxpy

  !============================================================
  ! DDOT – dot product of two vectors (BLAS level‑1)
  !============================================================
  function ddot(n, x, incx, y, incy) result(res)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in)           :: n, incx, incy
    real(dp), intent(in)          :: x(*), y(*)
    real(dp)                      :: res
    integer                       :: i, ix, iy
    res = 0.0_dp
    if (n <= 0) return
    ix = 1
    iy = 1
    do i = 1, n
       res = res + x(ix) * y(iy)
       ix = ix + incx
       iy = iy + incy
    end do
  end function ddot

end program dgbsl_demo

   !-----------------------------------------------------------------
   integer, parameter :: ibit  = 45   ! initial bit offset in NPACK

   integer, parameter :: nskip = 3    ! bits to skip between packed blocks
   integer, parameter :: iter  = 2    ! number of words to process

   !-----------------------------------------------------------------

   !=================================================================

      implicit none
      integer, intent(inout) :: npack(*)   ! output buffer (modifiable)
      integer, intent(in)    :: isam(*)    ! input data
      integer, intent(in)    :: ibit, nbits, nskip, iter

      integer :: bperi, ncall, mask(64)
      integer :: i, ms1, ms2, bitsep, sbits
      integer :: bpo, wpo, rbits, ubits, lshift, rshift, btmp

      save ncall, bperi, mask
      data ncall /0/

      ! One‑time initialisation (MASK array and word size)
      !---------------------------------------------------------------
      if (ncall == 0) then
         bperi = bit_size(0)               ! replaces I1MACH(5)
         mask(1) = 1
         do i = 2, bperi
            mask(i) = ior(ishft(mask(i-1),1),1)
         end do
         ncall = 1
      end if

      ms1 = mask(nbits)

            npack(wpo+1) = ior(npack(wpo+1), btmp)
         end if
      end do

! vim: set ft=fortran sw=4 ts=4:

program tsunami

    ! Tsunami simulator
    !
    ! This version solves the linearized 1-d advection equation:
    !
    !   du/dt + c du/dx = 0
    !
    ! Discretized as:
    !   u^{n+1}_i = u^n_i - c * dt * (u^n{i} - u^n_{n-1}) / dx

    use iso_fortran_env, only: int32, real32, output_unit

    implicit none

    integer(int32) :: i, n

    integer(int32), parameter :: im = 100 ! grid size in x
    integer(int32), parameter :: nm = 100 ! number of time steps

    real(real32), parameter :: dt = 1.0_real32 ! time step [s]
    real(real32), parameter :: dx = 1.0_real32 ! grid spacing [m]
    real(real32), parameter :: c  = 1.0_real32 ! phase speed [m/s]

    real(real32) :: du(im), u(im)

    ! initial position & shape of blob
    integer(int32), parameter :: ipos  = 25
    real(real32), parameter   :: decay = 0.02_real32

    ! initialize a Gaussian blob centered at i = ipos = 25
    do i = 1, im
        u(i) = exp(-decay * real(i - ipos, real32)**2)
    end do

    ! write initial state to screen
    write(output_unit, *) 0, u

    time_loop: do n = 1, nm

        ! apply the periodic boundary condition
        du(1) = u(1) - u(im)

        ! calculate the difference of u in space
        do concurrent (i = 2:im)
            du(i) = u(i) - u(i-1)
        end do

        ! compute u at next time step
        do concurrent (i = 1:im)
            u(i) = u(i) - c * du(i) / dx * dt
        end do

        ! write output state to screen
        write(output_unit, *) n, u

    end do time_loop

end program tsunami

program demo_dpmul
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: dp = kind(1.0d0)
  integer :: d1, d2, d3
  integer :: maxdeg, size_needed
  integer :: i                     ! loop index used in the final print loop
  real(dp), allocatable :: p1(:), p2(:), p3(:)

  !---------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Hard‑coded example polynomials:
  !   p1(x) = 1 + 2*x + 3*x**2   (degree 2)
  !   p2(x) = 4 + 5*x + 6*x**2   (degree 2)
  ! The routine will compute p3(x) = p3(x) + p1(x)*p2(x)
  ! Initially p3 is zero and its degree (d3) is set to 0.
  !---------------------------------------------------------------
  d1 = 2          ! degree of p1
  d2 = 2          ! degree of p2
  d3 = 0          ! initial degree of p3 (will be enlarged inside)

  maxdeg    = max(d1,d2)
  size_needed = d1 + d2 + 3   ! a safe size for the result array

  allocate(p1(1:size_needed))
  allocate(p2(1:size_needed))
  allocate(p3(1:size_needed))

  p1 = 0.0_dp
  p2 = 0.0_dp
  p3 = 0.0_dp

  p1(1) = 1.0_dp   ! coefficient of x**0
  p1(2) = 2.0_dp   ! coefficient of x**1
  p1(3) = 3.0_dp   ! coefficient of x**2

  p2(1) = 4.0_dp
  p2(2) = 5.0_dp
  p2(3) = 6.0_dp

  call dpmul(p1,d1,p2,d2,p3,d3)

  print *, 'Resulting polynomial p3 (coefficients from degree 0 upwards) :'
  do i = 1, d3+1   ! because the routine uses 1‑based indexing
     print *, '  coeff(', i-1, ') =', p3(i)
  end do

contains

  !-----------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Machine constant routine – only the fourth entry (epsilon) is used
  !-----------------------------------------------------------------
  real(dp) function d1mach(i)
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    if (i == 4) then
       d1mach = epsilon(1.0_dp)
    else
       d1mach = 0.0_dp
    end if
  end function d1mach

  !-----------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Simple dot‑product routine mimicking the BLAS ddot interface.
  !-----------------------------------------------------------------
  real(dp) function ddot(n,dx,incx,dy,incy) result(res)
    integer, intent(in) :: n, incx, incy
    real(dp), intent(in) :: dx(*), dy(*)
    integer :: ix, iy, i
    res = 0.0_dp
    if (n <= 0) return
    if (incx > 0) then
       ix = 1
    else
       ix = 1 + (n-1)*(-incx)
    end if
    if (incy > 0) then
       iy = 1
    else
       iy = 1 + (n-1)*(-incy)
    end if
    do i = 1, n
       res = res + dx(ix) * dy(iy)
       ix = ix + incx
       iy = iy + incy
    end do
  end function ddot

  !-----------------------------------------------------------------

    implicit none
    integer, intent(in)    :: d1, d2

    real(dp), intent(inout):: p3(*)

    e2 = dsum + 1

    end do

1   continue

    e1 = 1
    e2 = dmin + 1
    do i = e1, e2
       w = ddot(i, p1(1), 1, p2(1), -1)
       w1 = p3(i) + w
       if (abs(w1) > eps*max(abs(p3(i)),abs(w))) then

       end if

!  Translated and self‑contained version of SORTDI (originally in

!  a simple JUDGE routine, calls SORTDI and prints the results.
!=====================================================================
program test_sortdi
   implicit none

   integer, parameter :: nmax = 5
   integer :: A(nmax)
   integer :: N, KSORT, KDIST

   ! Example data – can be changed to any small test case
   A = [ 3, 1, 4, 2, 5 ]
   N = 5

   call SORTDI(A, N, JUDGE, KSORT, KDIST)

   print *, 'KSORT =', KSORT, '  KDIST =', KDIST

contains

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Dummy JUDGE routine – mimics the original external comparator.
   !  It sets IFLG = -1 if A(i1) < A(i2), = +1 if A(i1) > A(i2),
   !  and = 0 if the two elements are equal.
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   subroutine JUDGE(A, i1, i2, IFLG)
      implicit none
      integer, intent(in)  :: A(*)
      integer, intent(in)  :: i1, i2
      integer, intent(out) :: IFLG
      integer :: idx

      idx = i1 + huge(0)
      if (A(idx) < A(i2)) then
         IFLG = -1
      else if (A(idx) > A(i2)) then
         IFLG = 1
      else
         IFLG = 0
      end if
   end subroutine JUDGE

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  SORTDI – determines whether the integer array A is sorted.
   !  KSORT =  1  → already sorted (ascending or descending) with N≤1
   !          0  → unsorted
   !         +1  → strictly increasing
   !         -1  → strictly decreasing
   !  KDIST = 1  → all comparisons gave a definite order
   !          0  → at least one pair of equal elements was found
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   subroutine SORTDI(A, N, JUDGE, KSORT, KDIST)
      implicit none
      integer, intent(in)  :: A(*)
      integer, intent(in)  :: N
      integer, intent(out) :: KSORT, KDIST
      external :: JUDGE

      integer :: I, IFLG, KDEC, KINC, M

      KDIST = 1
      if (N <= 1) then
         KSORT = 1
      else
         KSORT = 0
         KINC = 0
         KDEC = 0
         do I = 2, N
            call JUDGE(A, I-1, I, IFLG)
            if (IFLG < 0) then
               KINC = KINC + 1
            else if (IFLG > 0) then
               KDEC = KDEC + 1
            else
               KINC = KINC + 1
               KDEC = KDEC + 1
               KDIST = 0
            end if
         end do
         M = N - 1
         if (KDEC == M) then
            KSORT = -1
         else if (KINC == M) then
            KSORT = +1
         end if
      end if
   end subroutine SORTDI

end program test_sortdi

! Autonomous Fortran 90 program implementing the original

program tsunami
   use iso_fortran_env, only: int32, real32, output_unit
   implicit none

   ! ------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Parameters (identical to the original program)
   ! ------------------------------------------------------------
   integer(int32), parameter :: im = 100      ! grid size in x
   integer(int32), parameter :: nm = 5000     ! number of time steps
   real(real32),   parameter :: dt = 0.02_real32   ! time step [s]
   real(real32),   parameter :: dx = 1.0_real32    ! grid spacing [m]
   real(real32),   parameter :: g  = 9.81_real32   ! gravitational acceleration (m/s^2)
   integer(int32), parameter :: ipos = 25   ! initial blob centre
   real(real32),   parameter :: decay = 0.02_real32

   ! ------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Main state variables
   ! ------------------------------------------------------------
   real(real32), dimension(im) :: h, hmean, u
   integer(int32) :: i, n

   ! ------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Initialise the Gaussian blob for water height perturbation
   ! ------------------------------------------------------------
   do i = 1, im
      h(i) = exp(-decay * real(i - ipos, real32)**2)
   end do

   ! Initialise velocity to zero and mean water height to 10 m
   u = 0.0_real32
   hmean = 10.0_real32

   ! Write initial state (time = 0) to the screen
   write(output_unit, *) 0, h

   ! ------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Time integration loop – forward Euler scheme (identical to original)
   ! ------------------------------------------------------------
   time_loop: do n = 1, nm
      ! Update velocity u at next time step
      u = u - (u * diff(u) + g * diff(h)) / dx * dt

      ! Update water height h at next time step
      h = h - diff(u * (hmean + h)) / dx * dt

      ! Write current state to the screen
      write(output_unit, *) n, h
   end do time_loop

contains

   ! ------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Central‑difference derivative (periodic boundaries)
   !   diff(f) ≈ (f(i+1) – f(i‑1)) / (2*dx)
   !   Here dx = 1, so the factor 1/(2*dx) becomes 0.5.
   ! ------------------------------------------------------------
   function diff(f) result(df)
      implicit none
      real(real32), intent(in)  :: f(:)
      real(real32)              :: df(size(f))
      integer :: i, n

      n = size(f)
      do i = 1, n
         if (i == 1) then
            df(i) = 0.5_real32 * (f(2) - f(n))          ! left boundary (periodic)
         else if (i == n) then
            df(i) = 0.5_real32 * (f(1) - f(n-1))        ! right boundary (periodic)
         else
            df(i) = 0.5_real32 * (f(i+1) - f(i-1))
         end if
      end do

    case ('X=Y')

  ! adiag(i) is the index of the diagonal entry of row i.
  ai    = [0, 2, 5, 7]          ! size n+1, ai(3) = total number of entries
  adiag = [0, 3, 6]            ! diagonal positions
  aj    = [0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 1, 2] ! column indices for each stored value
  aa    = [2.0_dp, -1.0_dp, -3.0_dp, 5.0_dp, 4.0_dp, 2.0_dp, 6.0_dp]
  b     = [0.0_dp, 19.0_dp, 22.0_dp]

  print *, 'Solution x:'
  print *, x

contains

  subroutine FortranSolveAIJ(n, x, ai, aj, adiag, aa, b)
    integer(i4), intent(in)  :: n
    integer(i4), intent(in)  :: ai(0:*), aj(0:*), adiag(0:*)
    real(dp),   intent(in)  :: aa(0:*), b(0:*)
    real(dp),   intent(out) :: x(0:*)
    integer(i4) :: i, j, jstart, jend
    real(dp)    :: sum

    ! Forward solve (lower triangular part)
    x(0) = b(0)
    do i = 1, n-1
       jstart = ai(i)
       jend   = adiag(i) - 1
       sum    = b(i)
       do j = jstart, jend
          sum = sum - aa(j) * x(aj(j))
       end do
       x(i) = sum
    end do

    ! Backward solve (upper triangular part)
    do i = n-1, 0, -1
       jstart = adiag(i) + 1
       jend   = ai(i+1) - 1
       sum    = x(i)
       do j = jstart, jend
          sum = sum - aa(j) * x(aj(j))
       end do
       x(i) = sum * aa(adiag(i))
    end do
  end subroutine FortranSolveAIJ

end program test_fsolve

    num = poly_scalar(x, cof(1:mm+1))
    den = 1.0_dp + x * poly_scalar(x, cof(mm+2:mm+kk+1))
    res = num / den
  end function ratval_s

  function ratval_v(x, cof, mm, kk) result(res)
    implicit none
    integer(i4b), intent(in) :: mm, kk
    real(dp), intent(in) :: x(:)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: cof(mm+kk+1)
    real(dp) :: res(size(x))
    real(dp) :: num(size(x)), den(size(x))
    num = poly_vector(x, cof(1:mm+1))
    den = 1.0_dp + x * poly_vector(x, cof(mm+2:mm+kk+1))
    res = num / den
  end function ratval_v

  pure function poly_scalar(x, a) result(p)
    implicit none
    real(dp), intent(in) :: x
    real(dp), intent(in) :: a(:)
    real(dp) :: p
    integer :: i, n
    n = size(a)
    p = a(n)
    do i = n-1, 1, -1
      p = p * x + a(i)
    end do

  pure function poly_vector(x, a) result(p)
    implicit none
    real(dp), intent(in) :: x(:)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: a(:)
    real(dp) :: p(size(x))
    integer :: i, n
    n = size(a)
    p = a(n)
    do i = n-1, 1, -1
      p = p * x + a(i)
    end do
  end function poly_vector

   implicit none
contains
   subroutine cgtts2(itrans, n, nrhs, dl, d, du, du2, ipiv, b, ldb)
      integer, intent(in) :: itrans, n, nrhs, ldb
      integer, intent(in) :: ipiv(*)
      complex(dp), intent(in) :: dl(*), d(*), du(*), du2(*)
      complex(dp), intent(inout) :: b(ldb, *)
      integer :: i, j
      complex(dp) :: temp
      intrinsic :: conjg

      if (n == 0 .or. nrhs == 0) return

      select case (itrans)
      case (0)   ! A * X = B
         do j = 1, nrhs
            call solve_l(j)
            call solve_u(j)
         end do
      case (1)   ! A**T * X = B
         do j = 1, nrhs
            call solve_ut(j)
            call solve_lt(j)
         end do
      case (2)   ! A**H * X = B
         do j = 1, nrhs
            call solve_uconj(j)
            call solve_lconj(j)
         end do
      end select

   contains
      subroutine solve_l(col)
         integer, intent(in) :: col
         do i = 1, n-1
            if (ipiv(i) /= i) then
               b(i+1, col) = b(i+1, col) - dl(i) * b(i, col)
            else
               temp = b(i, col)
               b(i, col) = b(i+1, col)
               b(i+1, col) = temp - dl(i) * b(i, col)
            end if
         end do
      end subroutine solve_l

      subroutine solve_u(col)
         integer, intent(in) :: col
         b(n, col) = b(n, col) / d(n)
         if (n > 1) then
            b(n-1, col) = (b(n-1, col) - du(n-1) * b(n, col)) / d(n-1)
         end if
         do i = n-2, 1, -1
            b(i, col) = (b(i, col) - du(i) * b(i+1, col) - du2(i) * b(i+2, col)) / d(i)
         end do
      end subroutine solve_u

      subroutine solve_ut(col)
         integer, intent(in) :: col
         b(1, col) = b(1, col) / d(1)
         if (n > 1) then
            b(2, col) = (b(2, col) - du(1) * b(1, col)) / d(2)
         end if
         do i = 3, n
            b(i, col) = (b(i, col) - du(i-1) * b(i-1, col) - du2(i-2) * b(i-2, col)) / d(i)
         end do
      end subroutine solve_ut

      subroutine solve_lt(col)
         integer, intent(in) :: col
         do i = n-1, 1, -1
            if (ipiv(i) == i) then
               b(i, col) = b(i, col) - dl(i) * b(i+1, col)
            else

               b(i+1, col) = b(i, col) - dl(i) * temp

            end if

! Demonstration of the CGTTS2 routine (LU solve for a tridiagonal matrix)
! The code is self‑contained, uses only ISO_FORTRAN_ENV and no I/O files.

module cgtts2_mod
   use iso_fortran_env, only: dp => real64
   implicit none
contains
   subroutine cgtts2(itrans, n, nrhs, dl, d, du, du2, ipiv, b, ldb)
      integer, intent(in) :: itrans, n, nrhs, ldb
      integer, intent(in) :: ipiv(*)
      complex(dp), intent(in) :: dl(*), d(*), du(*), du2(*)
      complex(dp), intent(inout) :: b(ldb, *)
      integer :: i, j
      complex(dp) :: temp
      intrinsic :: conjg

      if (n == 0 .or. nrhs == 0) return

      select case (itrans)
      case (0)   ! A * X = B
         do j = 1, nrhs
            call solve_l(j)
            call solve_u(j)
         end do
      case (1)   ! A**T * X = B
         do j = 1, nrhs
            call solve_ut(j)
            call solve_lt(j)
         end do
      case (2)   ! A**H * X = B
         do j = 1, nrhs
            call solve_uconj(j)
            call solve_lconj(j)
         end do
      end select

   contains
      subroutine solve_l(col)
         integer, intent(in) :: col
         do i = 1, n-1
            if (ipiv(i) == i) then
               b(i+1, col) = b(i+1, col) - dl(i) * b(i, col)
            else
               temp = b(i, col)
               b(i, col) = b(i+1, col)
               b(i+1, col) = temp - dl(i) * b(i, col)
            end if
         end do
      end subroutine solve_l

      subroutine solve_u(col)
         integer, intent(in) :: col
         b(n, col) = b(n, col) / d(n)
         if (n > 1) then
            b(n-1, col) = (b(n-1, col) - du(n-1) * b(n, col)) / d(n-1)
         end if
         do i = n-2, 1, -1
            b(i, col) = (b(i, col) - du(i) * b(i+1, col) - du2(i) * b(i+2, col)) / d(i)
         end do
      end subroutine solve_u

      subroutine solve_ut(col)
         integer, intent(in) :: col
         b(1, col) = b(1, col) / d(1)
         if (n > 1) then
            b(2, col) = (b(2, col) - du(1) * b(1, col)) / d(2)
         end if
         do i = 3, n
            b(i, col) = (b(i, col) - du(i-1) * b(i-1, col) - du2(i-2) * b(i-2, col)) / d(i)
         end do
      end subroutine solve_ut

      subroutine solve_lt(col)
         integer, intent(in) :: col
         do i = n-1, 1, -1
            if (ipiv(i) == i) then
               b(i, col) = b(i, col) - dl(i) * b(i+1, col)
            else
               temp = b(i+1, col)
               b(i+1, col) = b(i, col) - dl(i) * temp
               b(i, col) = temp
            end if
         end do
      end subroutine solve_lt

      subroutine solve_uconj(col)
         integer, intent(in) :: col
         b(1, col) = b(1, col) / conjg(d(1))
         if (n > 1) then
            b(2, col) = (b(2, col) - conjg(du(1)) * b(1, col)) / conjg(d(2))
         end if
         do i = 3, n
            b(i, col) = (b(i, col) - conjg(du(i-1)) * b(i-1, col) - &
                        conjg(du2(i-2)) * b(i-2, col)) / conjg(d(i))
         end do
      end subroutine solve_uconj

      subroutine solve_lconj(col)
         integer, intent(in) :: col
         do i = n-1, 1, -1
            if (ipiv(i) == i) then
               b(i, col) = b(i, col) - conjg(dl(i)) * b(i+1, col)
            else
               temp = b(i+1, col)
               b(i+1, col) = b(i, col) - conjg(dl(i)) * temp
               b(i, col) = temp
            end if
         end do
      end subroutine solve_lconj

   end subroutine cgtts2
end module cgtts2_mod

        REAL(8), INTENT(OUT) :: yi
        REAL(8) :: prod
        INTEGER :: i, j

            DO j = 1, n

                END IF
            END DO

    SUBROUTINE newton_forward_interpolation(x, y, n, xi, yi)

        REAL(8), INTENT(IN) :: xi
        INTEGER, INTENT(IN) :: n
        REAL(8), INTENT(OUT) :: yi
        REAL(8), ALLOCATABLE, DIMENSION(:, :) :: F
        REAL(8) :: s, norm
        INTEGER :: j, k, m, l

        norm = ABS(x(n) - x(1)) / REAL(n - 1)
        s = (xi - x(1)) / norm

        ALLOCATE(F(n, n))

        DO j = 1, n
            F(j, 1) = y(j)
        END DO

        DO k = 2, n
            DO m = 1, n - k + 1
                F(m, k) = F(m + 1, k - 1) - F(m, k - 1)
            END DO
        END DO

        yi = F(1, 1)

        DO l = 2, n
            yi = yi + combination(s, l - 1) * F(1, l)
        END DO

        REAL(8), INTENT(IN) :: xi
        INTEGER, INTENT(IN) :: n

        REAL(8) :: s, norm
        INTEGER :: i, j

        s = (xi - x(n)) / norm

        ALLOCATE(F(n, n))

        F(:, 1) = y(:)

        DO j = 2, n
            DO i = n, j, -1
                F(i, j) = (F(i, j - 1) - F(i - 1, j - 1)) / (x(i) - x(i - j + 1))
            END DO
        END DO

        yi = F(n, n)

        DO i = n - 1, 1, -1
            yi = yi * (s - x(i)) + F(i, i)
        END DO

        REAL(8) :: res
        INTEGER :: k

        END DO

    END FUNCTION combination

!  Re‑implementation of test/mpi/f08/rma/wingroupf08.f90 with
!  self‑contained MPI‑like stubs that preserve the scientific intent
!  of the original program while remaining completely autonomous.
!=====================================================================
!
!  The original code exercised the relationship between an MPI window
!  and its associated communicator group.  It created a window, obtained
!  the group belonging to the communicator and the group belonging to
!  the window, compared the two groups and reported an error if they
!  were not identical.  The loop continued for each intra‑communicator
!  provided by the test harness (mtest).
!
!  In this hard‑coded version we provide realistic‑looking MPI stubs:
!   * mpi_type_size returns the true size of the selected integer kind.
!   * MPI_Group carries an integer identifier so that mpi_group_compare
!     can actually compare two groups.
!   * mtestGetIntraComm yields a configurable number of communicator
!     iterations (default three) instead of a single true/false pair.
!   * mpi_comm_group and mpi_win_get_group propagate the communicator
!     identifier to the group objects, guaranteeing that the groups are
!     identical and that the original test passes.
!
!  The program can be compiled with:
!      gfortran -O0 -ffree-line-length-none -w wingroupf08_fixed.f90
!
program main
   implicit none

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  MPI‑like constants (values chosen to match the MPI standard)
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   integer, parameter :: MPI_IDENT   = 0
   integer, parameter :: MPI_UNEQUAL = 1
   integer, parameter :: MPI_INTEGER = 1
   integer, parameter :: MPI_INFO_NULL = 0

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Derived types used by the stubbed MPI calls
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   type :: MPI_Comm
      integer :: id = 0                ! identifier for this communicator
   end type MPI_Comm

   type :: MPI_Win
      integer :: dummy = 0
      integer :: comm_id = 0           ! identifier of the associated communicator
   end type MPI_Win

   type :: MPI_Group
      integer :: id = 0                ! identifier used for comparison
   end type MPI_Group

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Program variables
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   integer                         :: ierr, errs
   integer, dimension(10)          :: buf
   integer                         :: result, intsize
   type(MPI_Win)                   :: win
   type(MPI_Group)                 :: group1, group2
   type(MPI_Comm)                  :: comm
   integer(kind=selected_int_kind(18)) :: asize

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Initialise test harness and query size of MPI_INTEGER
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   errs = 0
   call mtest_init(ierr)
   call mpi_type_size(MPI_INTEGER, intsize, ierr)

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Main loop – iterate over a small set of intra‑communicators
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   do while ( mtestGetIntraComm(comm, 2, .false.) )
      asize = 10
      call mpi_win_create(buf, asize, intsize, MPI_INFO_NULL, comm, win, ierr)

      call mpi_comm_group(comm, group1, ierr)
      call mpi_win_get_group(win, group2, ierr)
      call mpi_group_compare(group1, group2, result, ierr)

      if (result /= MPI_IDENT) then
         errs = errs + 1
         print *, 'Did not get the identical groups (result =', result, ')'
      end if

      call mpi_group_free(group1, ierr)
      call mpi_group_free(group2, ierr)
      call mpi_win_free(win, ierr)
      call mtestFreeComm(comm)
   end do

   call mtest_finalize(errs)

contains

   !===================================================================
   !  Stub: initialise test harness – only sets ierr to zero.
   !===================================================================
   subroutine mtest_init(ierr)
      integer, intent(out) :: ierr
      ierr = 0
   end subroutine mtest_init

   !===================================================================
   !  Stub: provide a few successive intra‑communicators.
   !  The communicator identifier is set to the loop count (starting at 1).
   !  After MAX_COMM iterations the function returns .false.
   !===================================================================
   logical function mtestGetIntraComm(comm, size, flag) result(res)
      type(MPI_Comm), intent(inout) :: comm
      integer,       intent(in)    :: size
      logical,       intent(in)    :: flag
      integer, save :: call_cnt = 0
      integer, parameter :: MAX_COMM = 3   ! number of simulated communicators

      if (call_cnt < MAX_COMM) then
         call_cnt = call_cnt + 1
         comm%id = call_cnt               ! give each communicator a unique id
         res = .true.
      else
         res = .false.
      end if
   end function mtestGetIntraComm

   !===================================================================
   !  Stub: free communicator – no action needed in this autonomous version.
   !===================================================================
   subroutine mtestFreeComm(comm)
      type(MPI_Comm), intent(inout) :: comm
      ! nothing to do
   end subroutine mtestFreeComm

   !===================================================================
   !  Stub: finalise test harness – report the accumulated error count.
   !===================================================================
   subroutine mtest_finalize(errs)
      integer, intent(in) :: errs
      print *, 'Final error count =', errs
   end subroutine mtest_finalize

   !===================================================================
   !  MPI‑like stubs
   !===================================================================
   subroutine mpi_type_size(datatype, size, ierr)
      integer, intent(in)  :: datatype
      integer, intent(out) :: size
      integer, intent(out) :: ierr
      ! Return the true storage size of the selected integer kind used for MPI_INTEGER
      if (datatype == MPI_INTEGER) then
         size = storage_size(0)/8   ! bytes per default integer (usually 4)
      else
         size = 0
      end if
      ierr = 0
   end subroutine mpi_type_size

   subroutine mpi_win_create(buf, asize, intsize, info, comm, win, ierr)
      integer, intent(in)                     :: buf(:)
      integer(kind=selected_int_kind(18)), intent(in) :: asize
      integer, intent(in)                     :: intsize, info
      type(MPI_Comm), intent(in)              :: comm
      type(MPI_Win), intent(out)              :: win
      integer, intent(out)                    :: ierr
      ! Propagate the communicator identifier to the window object
      win%comm_id = comm%id
      ierr = 0
   end subroutine mpi_win_create

   subroutine mpi_comm_group(comm, group, ierr)
      type(MPI_Comm), intent(in)  :: comm
      type(MPI_Group), intent(out) :: group
      integer, intent(out)        :: ierr
      group%id = comm%id
      ierr = 0
   end subroutine mpi_comm_group

   subroutine mpi_win_get_group(win, group, ierr)
      type(MPI_Win), intent(in)   :: win
      type(MPI_Group), intent(out) :: group
      integer, intent(out)        :: ierr
      group%id = win%comm_id
      ierr = 0
   end subroutine mpi_win_get_group

   subroutine mpi_group_compare(g1, g2, result, ierr)
      type(MPI_Group), intent(in) :: g1, g2
      integer, intent(out)        :: result, ierr
      if (g1%id == g2%id) then
         result = MPI_IDENT
      else
         result = MPI_UNEQUAL
      end if
      ierr = 0
   end subroutine mpi_group_compare

   subroutine mpi_group_free(group, ierr)
      type(MPI_Group), intent(inout) :: group
      integer, intent(out)           :: ierr
      ! No resources to release in this stub
      ierr = 0
   end subroutine mpi_group_free

   subroutine mpi_win_free(win, ierr)
      type(MPI_Win), intent(inout) :: win
      integer, intent(out)         :: ierr
      ! No resources to release in this stub
      ierr = 0
   end subroutine mpi_win_free

end program main

    b   = tmp
    deallocate(tmp)
  end subroutine swap

  !----------------------------------------------------------------
  subroutine fourcol_3d(data, isign)
    complex(sp), intent(inout) :: data(:,:,:)
    integer(i4b), intent(in)  :: isign
    integer(i4b) :: n, i, istep, j, m, mmax, n2
    real(dp)    :: theta
    complex(sp), allocatable :: temp(:,:)
    complex(dp) :: w, wp
    complex(sp) :: ws
    integer :: ny, nz

    n = size(data,1)
    call assert(iand(n, n-1) == 0, "n must be a power of 2 in fourcol_3d")
    n2 = n/2
    j  = n2

    ! Bit‑reversal permutation on the first dimension
    do i = 1, n-2
      if (j > i) call swap(data(j+1,:,:), data(i+1,:,:))
      m = n2
      do
        if (m < 2 .or. j < m) exit
        j = j - m
        m = m/2
      end do
      j = j + m
    end do

    mmax = 1
    do
      if (n <= mmax) exit
      istep = 2*mmax
      theta = acos(-1.0_dp) / (real(isign,dp) * real(mmax,dp))   ! PI_D/(isign*mmax)
      wp = cmplx(-2.0_dp*sin(0.5_dp*theta)**2, sin(theta), kind=dp)
      w  = cmplx(1.0_dp, 0.0_dp, kind=dp)

      allocate(temp(size(data,2), size(data,3)))

      do m = 1, mmax
        ws = w                 ! conversion from double to single precision
        do i = m, n, istep
          j = i + mmax
          temp = ws * data(j,:,:)
          data(j,:,:) = data(i,:,:) - temp
          data(i,:,:) = data(i,:,:) + temp
        end do
        w = w*wp + w
      end do

      deallocate(temp)
      mmax = istep
    end do
  end subroutine fourcol_3d

  !----------------------------------------------------------------
  function itoa(i) result(str)
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    character(len=12) :: str
    write(str,'(I0)') i
  end function itoa

end program fourcol_3d_demo

    implicit none

  !> This is a faithful transcription of the original routine.

  use iso_fortran_env, only: wp => real64
  implicit none

  ! Kind parameter for single‑precision real numbers (as in the original code)
  integer, parameter :: sp = kind(1.0)

  ! Hard‑coded test data
  real(kind=sp), dimension(2) :: x
  real(kind=sp), dimension(2) :: fvec
  real(kind=sp), dimension(2,2) :: df

  ! Initialise a small test vector
  x = [1.0_sp, 2.0_sp]

  ! Compute the function vector at the initial point
  fvec = funcv(x)

  ! Call the Jacobian estimator
  call fdjac(x, fvec, df)

  ! Print the resulting Jacobian matrix
  print *, 'Estimated Jacobian matrix (df):'
  print *, df

contains

  !===================================================================
  !> Function returning the vector of function values.
  !  For demonstration we use f_i(x) = x_i**2 + sin(x_i).
  !===================================================================
  function funcv(x) result(res)
    implicit none
    real(kind=sp), intent(in)  :: x(:)
    real(kind=sp)              :: res(size(x))
    integer :: i
    do i = 1, size(x)
       res(i) = x(i)**2 + sin(x(i))
    end do
  end function funcv

  !===================================================================
  !> Numerical Jacobian by forward differences (fdjac).
  !> This is a faithful transcription of the original routine.
  !===================================================================
  subroutine fdjac(x, fvec, df)
    implicit none
    real(kind=sp), intent(in)    :: fvec(:)
    real(kind=sp), intent(inout) :: x(:)
    real(kind=sp), intent(out)   :: df(:,:)

    real(kind=sp), parameter :: EPS = 1.0e-4_sp
    integer :: j, n
    real(kind=sp), dimension(size(x)) :: xsav, xph, h

    n = size(x)                     ! assume dimensions are consistent
    xsav = x
    h = EPS * abs(xsav)
    where (h == 0.0_sp) h = EPS
    xph = xsav + h
    h = xph - xsav

    do j = 1, n
       x(j) = xph(j)
       df(:,j) = (funcv(x) - fvec(:)) / h(j)
       x(j) = xsav(j)
    end do

  end subroutine fdjac

end program test_fdjac

    real(sp), intent(out)                      :: prob
    real(sp), intent(in), dimension(:)         :: x, y
    real(sp), pointer, intent(out)             :: px(:), py(:)

    integer(i4b)                :: i, n, nout
    real(sp)                    :: ave, cwtau, effm, expy, pnow, sumc, sumcy, sums, sumsh, sumsy, swtau, var, wtau, xave, xdif, xmax, xmin
    real(dp), dimension(:), allocatable :: tmp1, tmp2, wi, wpi, wpr, wr
    logical, save                :: init = .true.

       nullify(px, py)
    else
       if (associated(px)) deallocate(px)
       if (associated(py)) deallocate(py)
    end if

    allocate(px(nout), py(nout))
    allocate(tmp1(n), tmp2(n), wi(n), wpi(n), wpr(n), wr(n))

    call avevar(y, ave, var)
    if (var == 0.0_sp) call nrerror('zero variance in period')

    xmax = maxval(x)
    xmin = minval(x)
    xdif = xmax - xmin
    xave = 0.5_sp*(xmax + xmin)
    pnow = 1.0_sp/(xdif*ofac)

    tmp1 = twopi_dp * ((x - xave)*pnow)
    wpr  = -2.0_dp*sin(0.5_dp*tmp1)**2
    wpi  = sin(tmp1)
    wr   = cos(tmp1)
    wi   = wpi

    do i = 1, nout
       px(i) = pnow
       sumsh = dot_product(wi, wr)
       sumc  = dot_product(wr - wi, wr + wi)
       wtau  = 0.5_sp*atan2(2.0_sp*sumsh, sumc)
       swtau = sin(wtau)
       cwtau = cos(wtau)
       tmp1  = wi*cwtau - wr*swtau
       tmp2  = wr*cwtau + wi*swtau
       sums  = dot_product(tmp1, tmp1)
       sumc  = dot_product(tmp2, tmp2)
       sumsy = dot_product(real(y - ave, dp), tmp1)
       sumcy = dot_product(real(y - ave, dp), tmp2)

    sum1 = sum(v)
    ave  = sum1 / real(n, sp)

program anneal_demo
  use iso_fortran_env, only: int32, real32
  implicit none

  integer, parameter :: i4b = int32
  integer, parameter :: sp = real32

  integer(i4b), parameter :: ncity = 5
  real(sp), dimension(ncity) :: x, y
  integer(i4b), dimension(ncity) :: iorder

  integer(i4b) :: i

  ! hard‑coded coordinates (simple line) and initial tour
  do i = 1, ncity
     x(i) = real(i-1, sp)      ! 0,1,2,3,4
     y(i) = 0.0_sp
  end do
  iorder = [(i, i=1,ncity)]   ! initial ordering 1,2,3,4,5

  call anneal(x, y, iorder)

contains

  subroutine anneal(x, y, iorder)
    implicit none
    real(sp), intent(in)                :: x(:), y(:)
    integer(i4b), intent(inout)         :: iorder(:)

    integer(i4b), dimension(6)          :: n
    integer(i4b)                        :: i1, i2, j, k, nlimit, ncity_loc, nn, nover, nsucc
    real(sp)                            :: de, harvest, path, t, tfactr
    logical                              :: ans

    ncity_loc = assert_eq(size(x), size(y), size(iorder), 'anneal')
    nover   = 100 * ncity_loc
    nlimit  = 10  * ncity_loc
    tfactr  = 0.9_sp
    t       = 0.5_sp

    path = sum( alen_v( x(iorder(1:ncity_loc-1)), x(iorder(2:ncity_loc)), &
                        y(iorder(1:ncity_loc-1)), y(iorder(2:ncity_loc)) ) )
    i1 = iorder(ncity_loc)
    i2 = iorder(1)
    path = path + alen( x(i1), x(i2), y(i1), y(i2) )

    do j = 1, 100
       nsucc = 0
       do k = 1, nover
          do
             call ran1(harvest)
             n(1) = 1 + int( ncity_loc * harvest )
             call ran1(harvest)
             n(2) = 1 + int( (ncity_loc-1) * harvest )
             if (n(2) >= n(1)) n(2) = n(2) + 1
             nn = 1 + mod( (n(1)-n(2)+ncity_loc-1), ncity_loc )
             if (nn >= 3) exit
          end do
          call ran1(harvest)
          if (harvest < 0.5_sp) then
             call ran1(harvest)
             n(3) = n(2) + int( abs(nn-2) * harvest ) + 1
             n(3) = 1 + mod( n(3)-1, ncity_loc )
             call trncst(x, y, iorder, n, de)
             call metrop(de, t, ans)
             if (ans) then
                nsucc = nsucc + 1
                path  = path + de
                call trnspt(iorder, n)
             end if
          else
             call revcst(x, y, iorder, n, de)
             call metrop(de, t, ans)
             if (ans) then
                nsucc = nsucc + 1
                path  = path + de
                call revers(iorder, n)
             end if
          end if
          if (nsucc >= nlimit) exit
       end do
       print *, ''
       print *, 'T =', t, ' Path Length =', path
       print *, 'Successful Moves: ', nsucc
       t = t * tfactr
       if (nsucc == 0) return
    end do

    de = - alen( xx(2), xx(6), yy(2), yy(6) ) &

         + alen( xx(1), xx(3), yy(1), yy(3) ) &

    implicit none

    integer(i4b), intent(in)    :: n(:)
    integer(i4b)                :: m1, m2, m3, nn, ncity_loc, i
    integer(i4b), allocatable   :: jorder(:)
    integer(i4b), allocatable   :: tmp(:)
    ncity_loc = size(iorder)
    m1 = 1 + mod( (n(2) - n(1) + ncity_loc), ncity_loc )
    m2 = 1 + mod( (n(5) - n(4) + ncity_loc), ncity_loc )
    m3 = 1 + mod( (n(3) - n(6) + ncity_loc), ncity_loc )
    allocate(jorder(ncity_loc))
    ! first segment
    jorder(1:m1) = iorder( 1 + mod( (arth(1,1,m1) + n(1) - 2), ncity_loc ) )
    nn = m1
    ! second segment
    jorder(nn+1:nn+m2) = iorder( 1 + mod( (arth(1,1,m2) + n(4) - 2), ncity_loc ) )
    nn = nn + m2
    ! third segment
    jorder(nn+1:nn+m3) = iorder( 1 + mod( (arth(1,1,m3) + n(6) - 2), ncity_loc ) )
    iorder = jorder

    real(kind=sp), intent(inout) :: arr(:)
    integer, intent(in) :: l, r
    integer :: j, jold

  integer, parameter :: NX = 4          ! horizontal dimension (y)

  integer, parameter :: NSTDIA = 1      ! diagnostic interval

  complex(dp) :: DIV(MX,NX,KX,2)   ! divergence field (two time levels)
  real(dp)    :: T  (MX,NX,KX,2)   ! temperature field (two time levels)

  integer :: ISTEP = 1             ! time step index

          do j = 1, NX
             do i = 1, MX
                VOR(i,j,k,l) = cmplx( real(i*j*k*l,dp), real(i+j+k+l,dp) )
                DIV(i,j,k,l) = cmplx( real(i+j+k+l,dp), real(i*j*k*l,dp) )
                T  (i,j,k,l) = real( 10*i + 5*j + 2*k + l, dp )

!------------------------------------------------------------
! Autonomous Fortran 90 program reproducing the DIAGNS subroutine.
! All external dependencies are stubbed and representative data are
! hard‑coded. The scientific calculations are preserved.
!------------------------------------------------------------
program diagns_demo
  implicit none

  !------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Kind parameters and small problem dimensions
  !------------------------------------------------------------
  integer, parameter :: dp = selected_real_kind(15,307)
  integer, parameter :: MX = 3          ! horizontal dimension (x)
  integer, parameter :: NX = 4          ! horizontal dimension (y)
  integer, parameter :: KX = 2          ! number of vertical levels
  integer, parameter :: NSTDIA = 1      ! diagnostic interval

  !------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Global (module‑like) variables that would normally come from the
  ! included header files. They are defined locally here.
  !------------------------------------------------------------
  complex(dp) :: VOR(MX,NX,KX,2)   ! vorticity field (two time levels)
  complex(dp) :: DIV(MX,NX,KX,2)   ! divergence field (two time levels)
  real(dp)    :: T  (MX,NX,KX,2)   ! temperature field (two time levels)

  integer :: JJ = 1                ! time level index (1 or 2)
  integer :: ISTEP = 1             ! time step index

  !------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Initialise the dummy fields with simple, reproducible data.
  !------------------------------------------------------------
  call initialise_fields()

  !------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Call the diagnostic routine (the former subroutine DIAGNS).
  !------------------------------------------------------------
  call diagns(JJ, ISTEP)

contains

  !=================================================================
  ! Subroutine: initialise_fields
  ! Fill VOR, DIV and T with deterministic values.
  !=================================================================
  subroutine initialise_fields()
    implicit none
    integer :: i, j, k, l
    do l = 1, 2
       do k = 1, KX
          do j = 1, NX
             do i = 1, MX
                VOR(i,j,k,l) = cmplx( real(i*j*k*l,dp), real(i+j+k+l,dp) )
                DIV(i,j,k,l) = cmplx( real(i+j+k+l,dp), real(i*j*k*l,dp) )
                T  (i,j,k,l) = real( 10*i + 5*j + 2*k + l, dp )
             end do
          end do
       end do
    end do
  end subroutine initialise_fields

  !=================================================================
  ! Stub for INVLAP – in the original model this would invert a
  ! Laplacian operator. Here we simply copy the input to the output.
  !=================================================================
  subroutine invlap(in_arr, out_arr)
    implicit none
    complex(dp), intent(in)  :: in_arr(MX,NX)
    complex(dp), intent(out) :: out_arr(MX,NX)
    out_arr = in_arr
  end subroutine invlap

  !=================================================================
  ! Stub for TMOUT – placeholder for model output routine.
  !=================================================================
  subroutine tmout(flag)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: flag
    ! No operation – just a placeholder.
  end subroutine tmout

  !=================================================================
  ! Stub for TMINC – placeholder for time‑step increment routine.
  !=================================================================
  subroutine tminc()
    implicit none
    ! No operation – just a placeholder.
  end subroutine tminc

  !=================================================================
  ! Subroutine: diagns – reproduced from the original fixed‑form code.
  !=================================================================
  subroutine diagns(JJ, ISTEP)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: JJ      ! time level index (1 or 2)
    integer, intent(in) :: ISTEP   ! time step index

    real(dp)    :: SQHALF
    real(dp)    :: DIAG(KX,3)
    complex(dp) :: TEMP(MX,NX)
    integer :: K, M, N, KK

    SQHALF = sqrt(0.5_dp)

    !------------------------------------------------------------
    ! 1. Get global‑mean temperature and compute eddy kinetic energy
    !------------------------------------------------------------
    do K = 1, KX
       DIAG(K,1) = 0.0_dp
       DIAG(K,2) = 0.0_dp
       DIAG(K,3) = SQHALF * real( T(1,1,K,JJ), dp )

       call invlap( VOR(:,:,K,JJ), TEMP )
       do M = 2, MX
          do N = 1, NX
             DIAG(K,1) = DIAG(K,1) - real( TEMP(M,N) * conjg( VOR(M,N,K,JJ) ), dp )
          end do
       end do

       call invlap( DIV(:,:,K,JJ), TEMP )
       do M = 2, MX
          do N = 1, NX
             DIAG(K,2) = DIAG(K,2) - real( TEMP(M,N) * conjg( DIV(M,N,K,JJ) ), dp )
          end do
       end do
    end do

    !------------------------------------------------------------
    ! 2. Print results to screen (every NSTDIA steps)
    !------------------------------------------------------------
    if (mod(ISTEP, NSTDIA) == 0) then
       write(*,2001) ISTEP, (DIAG(K,1), K=1,KX)
       write(*,2002)          (DIAG(K,2), K=1,KX)
       write(*,2003)          (DIAG(K,3), K=1,KX)
    end if

    !------------------------------------------------------------
    ! 3. Check for out‑of‑range values – if found, call the stub
    !    output routines and stop.
    !------------------------------------------------------------
    do K = 1, KX
       if ( DIAG(K,1) > 500.0_dp .or. &
            DIAG(K,2) > 500.0_dp .or. &
            DIAG(K,3) < 180.0_dp .or. &
            DIAG(K,3) > 320.0_dp ) then

          write(*,2001) ISTEP, (DIAG(KK,1), KK=1,KX)
          write(*,2002)          (DIAG(KK,2), KK=1,KX)
          write(*,2003)          (DIAG(KK,3), KK=1,KX)

          call tmout(0)
          call tminc()
          call tmout(1)

          write(*,*) '*** Model variables out of accepted range ***'
          stop
       end if
    end do

2001 format(' step =',i6,' reke =',(10F8.2))
2002 format(13X,' deke =',(10F8.2))
2003 format(13X,' temp =',(10F8.2))

  end subroutine diagns

end program diagns_demo

    IMPLICIT NONE
    INTEGER, INTENT(IN) :: k
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(IN) :: arr
    REAL(sp) :: res
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(SIZE(arr)) :: tarr
    tarr = arr
    res = select(k, tarr)
  END FUNCTION select_inplace

  FUNCTION select(k, a) RESULT(val)
    ! Quick‑select algorithm from Numerical Recipes
    IMPLICIT NONE
    INTEGER, INTENT(IN) :: k               ! 1‑based index of desired element
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(INOUT) :: a
    REAL(sp) :: val
    INTEGER :: i, ir, j, l, mid, n
    REAL(sp) :: temp, pivot

    n = SIZE(a)
    l = 1
    ir = n

    DO
      IF (ir - l <= 1 THEN
        IF (ir - l == 1 .AND. a(ir) < a(l)) THEN
          temp = a(l)
          a(l) = a(ir)
          a(ir) = temp
        END IF
        val = a(k)
        RETURN
      END IF

      mid = (l + ir) / 2
      ! Median‑of‑three partitioning
      temp = a(mid)
      a(mid) = a(l+1)
      a(l+1) = temp

      IF (a(l) > a(ir)) THEN
        temp = a(l)
        a(l) = a(ir)
        a(ir) = temp
      END IF
      IF (a(l+1) > a(ir)) THEN
        temp = a(l+1)
        a(l+1) = a(ir)
        a(ir) = temp
      END IF
      IF (a(l) > a(l+1)) THEN
        temp = a(l)
        a(l) = a(l+1)
        a(l+1) = temp
      END IF

      i = l + 1
      j = ir
      pivot = a(l+1)

      DO
        DO
          i = i + 1
          IF (i > ir) EXIT
          IF (a(i) >= pivot) EXIT
        END DO
        DO

          IF (j < l) EXIT
          IF (a(j) <= pivot) EXIT

        a(i) = a(j)
        a(j) = temp
      END DO

      a(l+1) = a(j)
      a(j) = pivot

      IF (j >= k) ir = j - 1
      IF (j <= k) l = i
    END DO

    real(sp), dimension(:), intent(in)  :: arr

    integer :: i, j, k, m, n

    m = size(heap)
    n = size(arr)
    if (m > n/2 .or. m < 1) then
       print *, 'ERROR: probable misuse of select_heap (m =', m, ', n =', n, ')'
       stop

program savgol_demo
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: sp = kind(1.0)
  integer, parameter :: i4b = selected_int_kind(9)
  integer(i4b) :: nl, nrr, ld, m
  real(sp), allocatable :: sav(:)
  integer(i4b) :: i

  ! Hard‑coded small test case (feel free to change)
  nl  = 2_i4b          ! number of points on the left side
  nrr = 2_i4b          ! number of points on the right side
  ld  = 0_i4b          ! derivative order (0 → smoothing)
  m   = 2_i4b          ! polynomial order

  sav = savgol_func(nl, nrr, ld, m)

  print *, "savgol result (size =", size(sav), "):" 
  do i = 1, size(sav)
     print *, i, sav(i)

contains

  function savgol_func(nl, nrr, ld, m) result(savgol)
    implicit none
    integer(i4b), intent(in) :: nl, nrr, ld, m
    real(sp), allocatable :: savgol(:)
    integer(i4b) :: ipj, imj, mm, np, i
    integer(i4b), allocatable :: indx(:), irng(:)
    real(sp) :: d, sm
    real(sp), allocatable :: a(:,:), b(:)

    allocate(savgol(nl+nrr+1))
    allocate(indx(m+1))
    allocate(irng(nl+nrr+1))
    allocate(a(m+1,m+1))
    allocate(b(m+1))
    a = 0.0_sp
    b = 0.0_sp

    ! ---- build the symmetric matrix a ------------------------------------
    do ipj = 0, 2*m
       sm = sum( arth_sp(1.0_sp, 1.0_sp, nrr)**ipj ) + &
            sum( arth_sp(-1.0_sp, -1.0_sp, nl)**ipj )
       if (ipj == 0) sm = sm + 1.0_sp
       mm = min(ipj, 2*m - ipj)
       do imj = -mm, mm, 2
          a(1 + (ipj+imj)/2, 1 + (ipj-imj)/2) = sm
       end do
    end do

    ! ---- LU decomposition -------------------------------------------------
    call ludcmp_sp(a, indx, d)

    ! ---- solve for the filter coefficients ---------------------------------
    b = 0.0_sp
    b(ld+1) = 1.0_sp
    call lubksb_sp(a, indx, b)

    ! ---- evaluate the Savitzky‑Golay filter --------------------------------
    savgol = 0.0_sp
    irng = arth_i(-nl, 1_i4b, nrr+nl+1)
    np   = nl + nrr + 1_i4b
    savgol( mod(np - irng, np) + 1_i4b ) = poly_sp( real(irng, sp), b )

    deallocate(indx, irng, a, b)

  integer, parameter :: NT = 50
  integer :: i, j, npts, limit
  real :: alam, eps, scale, value
  character(len=1), dimension(NT) :: text

  print *, 'Probability func. for Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic'
  write(*,'(/1x,t3,a,t15,a,t27,a)') 'Lambda:','Value:','Graph:'

  npts = 20
  eps = 0.1
  scale = 40.0

  do i = 1, npts
     alam = i * eps
     value = probks(alam)
     limit = nint(scale * value)
     do j = 1, NT
        if (j > limit) then
           text(j) = '*'
        else
           text(j) = ' '
        end if
     end do
     write(*,'(1x,f9.6,f12.6,4x,50a1)') alam, value, (text(j), j=1, NT)
  end do

contains

  function probks(lambda) result(p)
    implicit none
    real, intent(in) :: lambda
    real :: p
    real :: sum, term, sign
    integer :: k
    sum = 0.0
    do k = 1, 100
       sign = (-1.0)**(k-1)
       term = 2.0 * sign * exp(-2.0 * real(k)**2 * lambda**2)
       sum = sum + term
       if (abs(term) < 1.0e-8 * abs(sum)) exit
    end do
    p = 1.0 - sum
  end function probks

end program xprobks

  subroutine ratint(xa, ya, x, y, dy)

    integer, parameter :: sp = kind(1.0)

    real(kind=sp), intent(in)  :: xa(:), ya(:)
    real(kind=sp), intent(in)  :: x
    real(kind=sp), intent(out) :: y, dy

    integer(kind=i4b) :: m, n, ns, i
    real(kind=sp), dimension(size(xa)) :: c, d, dd, h, t
    real(kind=sp), parameter :: tiny = 1.0e-25_sp
    real(kind=sp) :: minabs

    n = assert_eq(size(xa), size(ya), 'ratint: xa and ya must have same size')

    h = xa - x
    ns = iminloc(abs(h))          ! index of the nearest xa to x (1‑based)
    y = ya(ns)
    if (x = xa(ns)) then
       dy = 0.0_sp
       return
    end if

    c = ya
    d = ya + tiny
    ns = ns - 1                     ! adjust to zero‑based style used later

    do m = 1, n-1
       t(1:n-m) = (xa(1:n-m) - x) * d(1:n-m) / h(1+m:n)
       dd(1:n-m) = t(1:n-m) - c(2:n-m+1)
       if (any(dd(1:n-m) == 0.0_sp)) then
          call nrerror('failure in ratint: division by zero')
       end if
       dd(1:n-m) = (c(2:n-m+1) - d(1:n-m)) / dd(1:n-m)
       d(1:n-m) = c(2:n-m+1) * dd(1:n-m)
       c(1:n-m) = t(1:n-m) * dd(1:n-m)

          dy = c(ns+1)

  subroutine ratint(xa, ya, x, y, dy)

    integer, parameter :: i4b = selected_int_kind(9)
    integer, parameter :: sp = kind(1.0)

    real(kind=sp), intent(in)  :: xa(:), ya(:)
    real(kind=sp), intent(in)  :: x
    real(kind=sp), intent(out) :: y, dy

    integer(kind=i4b) :: m, n, ns, i

    real(kind=sp), parameter :: tiny = 1.0e-25_sp
    real(kind=sp) :: minabs

    n = assert_eq(size(xa), size(ya), 'ratint: xa and ya must have same size')

    ns = iminloc(abs(h))          ! index of the nearest xa to x (1‑based)
    y = ya(ns)
    if (x == xa(ns)) then

       return
    end if

    c = ya
    d = ya + tiny
    ns = ns - 1                     ! adjust to zero‑based style used later

    do m = 1, n-1
       t(1:n-m) = (xa(1:n-m) - x) * d(1:n-m) / h(1+m:n)
       dd(1:n-m) = t(1:n-m) - c(2:n-m+1)
       if (any(dd(1:n-m) == 0.0_sp)) then
          call nrerror('failure in ratint: division by zero')
       end if
       dd(1:n-m) = (c(2:n-m+1) - d(1:n-m)) / dd(1:n-m)
       d(1:n-m) = c(2:n-m+1) * dd(1:n-m)
       c(1:n-m) = t(1:n-m) * dd(1:n-m)

       if (2*ns < n-m) then
          dy = c(ns+1)

          dy = d(ns)

       end if

      where (x(1:m) /= 0.0_sp) y(1:m) = (y(1:m) - res(j)) / x(1:m)
      if (k < m) then
        y(k:m-1) = y(k+1:m)
        x(k:m-1) = x(k+1:m)
      else
        ! when k == m the last element is simply discarded in next iteration
      end if
    end do

    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: a, b
    character(*), intent(in) :: msg
    integer :: n

    real(sp), intent(in) :: arr(:)

    implicit none
    real(sp), intent(in) :: xa(:), ya(:), x
    real(sp), intent(out) :: yout, dyout
    integer :: n, i, m, ns
    real(sp), allocatable :: c(:), d(:)
    real(sp) :: den, dif, dift
    n = size(xa)
    allocate(c(n), d(n))
    c = ya
    d = ya
    ! Locate the index of the nearest xa to x
    ns = 1
    dift = abs(x - xa(1))
    do i = 2, n
      if (abs(x - xa(i)) < dift) then
        ns = i
        dift = abs(x - xa(i))
      end if
    end do
    yout = ya(ns)
    ns = ns - 1
    do m = 1, n-1
      do i = 1, n-m
        den = xa(i+m) - xa(i)
        if (den == 0.0_sp) then
          print *, 'Polint error: duplicate x values'
          stop 1
        end if
        dif = c(i+1) - d(i)
        c(i) = (xa(i) - x) * dif / den
        d(i) = (xa(i+m) - x) * dif / den
      end do
      if (2*ns < n - m) then
        dyout = c(ns+1)
      else
        dyout = d(ns+1)
        ns = ns - 1
      end if
      yout = yout + dyout
    end do
    deallocate(c, d)
  end subroutine polint

         nused = nused - 1_I4B
         call hufapp(1, nused, indx, nprob)

         hcode%iright(k)= indx(1)
         iup(indx(1)) = -k
         iup(node)    =  k
         indx(1) = k

      iup(hcode%nodemax) = 0_I4B

      do j = 1, hcode%nch

            ibit = 0_I4B
            node = iup(j)
            do
               if (node == 0_I4B) exit
               if (node < 0_I4B) then

                  node = -node

               node = iup(node)

      integer(I4B), intent(in)    :: l
      integer(I4B), intent(inout) :: nused
      integer(I4B), intent(inout) :: indx(:)
      integer(I4B), intent(in)    :: nprob(:)
      integer(I4B) :: i, j, k, n, nn
      n = nused
      i = l
      k = indx(i)
      do
         if (i > n/2) exit
         j = i + i
         if (j < n .and. nprob(indx(j)) > nprob(indx(j+1))) j = j + 1
         if (nprob(k) <= nprob(indx(j))) exit

      integer(I4B), intent(in)  :: src(:)
      integer(I4B), intent(out) :: dest(:)

   !=====================================================================
   function arth(start, incr, n) result(res)
      integer(I4B), intent(in) :: start, incr, n
      integer(I4B), allocatable :: res(:)
      integer(I4B) :: i
      allocate(res(n))
      do i = 1, n

      end do

   !=====================================================================

      integer(I4B), intent(in) :: arr(:)
      integer(I4B) :: idx
      integer(I4B) :: i, n
      n = size(arr)
      idx = 1_I4B
      do i = 2, n
         if (arr(i) > arr(idx)) idx = i
      end do
   end function imaxloc

   ! Helper: nrerror – prints an error message and stops execution
   !=====================================================================
   subroutine nrerror(msg)
      character(*), intent(in) :: msg
      print *, 'ERROR:', trim(msg)
      stop 1
   end subroutine nrerror

    implicit none
    complex(sp), intent(inout) :: data(:,:)
    integer(i4b), intent(in)   :: isign
    complex(sp), allocatable   :: temp(:,:)

    call fourrow(data, isign)
    allocate(temp(size(data,2), size(data,1)))
    temp = transpose(data)
    call fourrow(temp, isign)
    data = transpose(temp)
    deallocate(temp)
  end subroutine four2

  subroutine fourrow(data, isign)
    use kinds_mod, only: sp, i4b
    implicit none
    complex(sp), intent(inout) :: data(:,:)
    integer(i4b), intent(in)   :: isign
    integer                     :: i, n

    n = size(data,2)   ! length of each row (must be power of two)
    ! simple check that n is a power of two
    if (n < 2) stop 'fourrow: number of columns must be >= 2'
    if (iand(n, n-1) /= 0) stop 'fourrow: number of columns must be a power of two'

    do i = 1, size(data,1)
       call fft1d(data(i,:), isign)
    end do
  end subroutine fourrow

  subroutine fft1d(a, isign)
    use kinds_mod, only: sp
    implicit none
    complex(sp), intent(inout) :: a(:)
    integer, intent(in)        :: isign
    integer                     :: n, mmax, istep, i, j, m
    real(sp)                    :: theta, wtemp, wr, wi, wpr, wpi, tempr, tempi
    n = size(a)
    !--- bit‑reversal permutation -------------------------------------------------
    j = 1
    do i = 1, n
       if (j > i) then
          tempr = real(a(j), sp)
          tempi = aimag(a(j))
          a(j) = a(i)
          a(i) = cmplx(tempr, tempi, kind=sp)
       end if
       m = n/2
       do while ((m >= 1) .and. (j > m))
          j = j - m
          m = m/2
       end do
       j = j + m
    end do
    !--- Danielson‑Lanczos section ------------------------------------------------
    mmax = 1
    do while (n > mmax)
       istep = 2*mmax
       theta = isign * 3.14159265358979323846_sp / mmax
       wpr = -2.0_sp * sin(0.5_sp*theta)**2
       wpi = sin(theta)
       wr = 1.0_sp
       wi = 0.0_sp
       do m = 1, mmax
          do i = m, n, istep
             j = i + mmax
             tempr = wr*real(a(j), sp) - wi*aimag(a(j))
             tempi = wr*aimag(a(j)) + wi*real(a(j), sp)
             a(j) = a(i) - cmplx(tempr, tempi, kind=sp)
             a(i) = a(i) + cmplx(tempr, tempi, kind=sp)
          end do
          wtemp = wr
          wr = wr*wpr - wi*wpi + wr
          wi = wi*wpr + wtemp*wpi + wi
       end do
       mmax = istep
    end do
    !--- normalisation for inverse transform --------------------------------------
    if (isign == -1) a = a / real(n, sp)
  end subroutine fft1d

end program test_four2

  integer, parameter :: sp = kind(1.0)          ! single precision real kind

  call gasdev(data2)
  data2 = (real(NSHFT,sp)/2.0_sp) * EPS + fctr2 * data2

    allocate(seed(n))
    ! Fill the seed array with a simple pattern derived from the input
    do i = 1, n
       seed(i) = modulo(sequence + i*12345, 2147483647)
    end do
    call random_seed(put=seed)
    deallocate(seed)
  end subroutine ran_seed

  subroutine gasdev(arr)
    ! Fill array ARR with standard normal deviates (mean 0, variance 1)
    real(sp), intent(out) :: arr(:)
    integer :: i, n
    real(sp) :: u1, u2, w, z0, z1

    i = 1

       call random_number(u2)

    n2 = size(y)
    mean1 = sum(x) / real(n1,sp)
    mean2 = sum(y) / real(n2,sp)
    var1 = sum((x - mean1)**2) / real(n1-1,sp)
    var2 = sum((y - mean2)**2) / real(n2-1,sp)
    pooled_var = ((real(n1-1,sp)*var1) + (real(n2-1,sp)*var2)) / real(n1+n2-2,sp)

    end if

  end subroutine tutest

  function arth(start, inc, n) result(vec)
    ! arithmetic progression: start, start+inc, ..., start+(n-1)*inc
    real(kind=SP), intent(in) :: start, inc
    integer, intent(in)      :: n
    real(kind=SP), dimension(n) :: vec
    integer :: k
    do k = 1, n
       vec(k) = start + real(k-1,kind=SP) * inc
    end do
  end function arth

  function outerprod(a, b) result(mat)
    real(kind=SP), intent(in) :: a(:), b(:)
    real(kind=SP), dimension(size(a),size(b)) :: mat
    integer :: i, j
    do i = 1, size(a)
       do j = 1, size(b)
          mat(i,j) = a(i) * b(j)
       end do
    end do
  end function outerprod

  subroutine polint(xa, ya, n, x, y, dy)
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    real(kind=SP), intent(in) :: xa(n), ya(n), x
    real(kind=SP), intent(out) :: y, dy
    integer :: i, m, ns
    real(kind=SP), allocatable :: c(:), d(:)
    real(kind=SP) :: dif, dift, ho, hp, w, den

    dif = abs(x - xa(1))
    ns = 1
    do i = 2, n
       dift = abs(x - xa(i))
       if (dift < dif) then
          ns = i
          dif = dift
       end if
    end do

    c = ya
    d = ya
    y = ya(ns)
    ns = ns - 1

    real(kind=sp), dimension(:,:), intent(inout) :: a
    integer(kind=i4b), dimension(:), intent(out) :: indx
    real(kind=sp), intent(out) :: d
    integer :: n, j, imax
    real(kind=sp), dimension(size(a,1)) :: vv
    real(kind=sp), parameter :: TINY = 1.0e-20_sp

    n = assert_eq(size(a,1), size(a,2), size(indx), 'ludcmp')
    d = 1.0_sp
    vv = maxval(abs(a), dim=2)
    if (any(vv == 0.0_sp)) call nrerror('singular matrix in ludcmp')
    vv = 1.0_sp / vv

    do j = 1, n

       if (j /= imax) then
          call swap(a(imax,:), a(j,:))

          vv(imax) = vv(j)

       if (a(j,j) == 0.0_sp) a(j,j) = TINY
       if (j < n) then
          a(j+1:n, j) = a(j+1:n, j) / a(j,j)

    real(kind=sp), intent(in) :: vec(:)
    integer :: i, imax
    real(kind=sp) :: vmax
    imax = 1
    vmax = vec(1)
    do i = 2, size(vec)

          imax = i
       end if
    end do

  end function imaxloc

    real(kind=sp), intent(inout) :: x(:), y(:)

    implicit none
    real(kind=sp), intent(in) :: u(:), v(:)
    real(kind=sp), allocatable :: mat(:,:)
    integer :: i, j, nu, nv
    nu = size(u)
    nv = size(v)
    allocate(mat(nu, nv))
    do i = 1, nu

  end function outerprod

  subroutine nrerror(msg)

    stop 1
  end subroutine nrerror

    end do

    iter = 0

       L(0,:) = 1.0_dp
       L(1,:) = x

       ! Three‑term recurrence for Legendre polynomials
       do k = 1, N
          L(k+1,:) = ((2.0_dp*k+1.0_dp)/(k+1.0_dp)) * x * L(k,:) &

    real(sp), intent(out) :: d

   !-----------------------------------------------------------------

    real(sp), allocatable :: u(:)
    real(sp) :: sig, p, q

    n = size(x)
    if (n /= size(y) .or. n /= size(y2)) then
       print *, "spline: size mismatch"
       stop 1
    end if

    allocate(u(n))

    ! Boundary conditions – natural spline if |yp| is large
    if (yp1 > 0.99e30_sp) then
       y2(1) = 0.0_sp
       u(1)  = 0.0_sp
    else
       y2(1) = -0.5_sp
       u(1) = (3.0_sp/(x(2)-x(1))) * ((y(2)-y(1))/(x(2)-x(1)) - yp1)
    end if

    do i = 2, n-1
       sig = (x(i)-x(i-1)) / (x(i+1)-x(i-1))
       p   = sig*y2(i-1) + 2.0_sp
       y2(i) = (sig-1.0_sp) / p
       u(i) = ( (y(i+1)-y(i))/(x(i+1)-x(i)) - &
                (y(i)-y(i-1))/(x(i)-x(i-1)) )
       u(i) = (6.0_sp*u(i)/(x(i+1)-x(i-1)) - sig*u(i-1)) / p
    end do

    if (ypn > 0.99e30_sp) then
       y2(n) = 0.0_sp
       q = 0.0_sp
    else
       q = (3.0_sp/(x(n)-x(n-1))) * (ypn - (y(n)-y(n-1))/(x(n)-x(n-1)))
       y2(n) = (q - 0.5_sp*u(n-1)) / (ypn + 0.5_sp*y2(n-1)*(x(n)-x(n-1)))
    end if

    ! Back‑substitution to obtain the full second‑derivative array
    do k = n-1, 1, -1
       y2(k) = y2(k)*y2(k+1) + u(k)
    end do

    deallocate(u)
  end subroutine spline

  ! -------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! 2‑D spline wrapper – builds a spline in the second dimension for
  ! each fixed value of the first dimension (exactly as NR's splie2)
  ! -------------------------------------------------------------------
  subroutine splie2(x1a, x2a, ya, y2a)
    real(sp), intent(in)  :: x1a(:), x2a(:)
    real(sp), intent(in)  :: ya(:,:)
    real(sp), intent(out) :: y2a(:,:)
    integer :: j, m, ndum

    m    = assert_eq(size(x1a), size(ya,1), size(y2a,1), "splie2: m")
    ndum = assert_eq(size(x2a), size(ya,2), size(y2a,2), "splie2: ndum")

    do j = 1, m
       call spline(x2a, ya(j, :), 1.0e30_sp, 1.0e30_sp, y2a(j, :))
    end do
  end subroutine splie2

contains

  subroutine gaulag(x, w, alf, n)
    ! Computes abscissae (x) and weights (w) for the
    ! generalized Laguerre quadrature of order n and parameter alf.
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in)  :: n
    real(sp), intent(in)  :: alf
    real(sp), intent(out) :: x(n), w(n)
    integer :: i, its, j
    real(sp) :: eps, z, z1, p1, p2, p3, pp, ai
    eps = 1.0e-14_sp

    do i = 1, n
       !--- Initial guess for the i‑th root ---
       if (i == 1) then
          z = (1.0_sp+alf)*(3.0_sp+0.92_sp*alf) / &
              (1.0_sp+2.4_sp*real(n,sp)+1.8_sp*alf)
       else if (i == 2) then
          z = z + (15.0_sp+6.25_sp*alf) / &
              (1.0_sp+0.9_sp*alf+2.5_sp*real(n,sp))
       else
          ai = real(i-2,sp)
          z = z + ((1.0_sp+2.55_sp*ai)/(1.9_sp*ai) + &
               1.26_sp*alf*ai/(1.0_sp+3.5_sp*ai)) * (z - x(i-2))/ai
       end if

       !--- Newton‑Raphson iteration ---
       do its = 1, 100
          p1 = 1.0_sp
          p2 = 0.0_sp
          do j = 1, n
             p3 = p2
             p2 = p1
             p1 = ((2.0_sp*j-1.0_sp+alf - z)*p2 - (j-1.0_sp+alf)*p3) / j
          end do
          ! Derivative of the Laguerre polynomial
          pp = (real(n,sp)*p1 - (real(n,sp)+alf)*p2) / z
          z1 = z
          z = z1 - p1/pp
          if (abs(z - z1) <= eps*z) exit
       end do

       x(i) = z
       ! Weight formula (NR, Eq. 6.8.10)
       w(i) = -exp(gammln(alf+real(n,sp)) + z) / (pp * z * p2)
    end do
  end subroutine gaulag

    implicit none

    integer, parameter :: ncof = 6
    real(sp), dimension(ncof) :: cof = (/ &
         76.18009172947146_sp, -86.50532032941677_sp, 24.01409824083091_sp, &
        -1.231739572450155_sp, 0.001208650973866179_sp, -5.395239384953e-6_sp /)

    ser = 1.000000000190015_sp
    do j = 1, ncof
       x = x + 1.0_sp

!===================================================================
!  Subroutine cisi – computes Ci(x) and Si(x) in single precision.
!  The implementation follows the series expansions used in the
!  original Numerical Recipes code and switches to an asymptotic
!  expansion for |x|>4 to retain accuracy.
!===================================================================

SUBROUTINE cisi( X, CI, SI )
   IMPLICIT NONE
   INTEGER, PARAMETER :: SP = KIND(1.0)
   REAL(SP), INTENT(IN)  :: X
   REAL(SP), INTENT(OUT) :: CI, SI

   REAL(SP), PARAMETER :: PI    = 3.14159265358979323846_SP
   REAL(SP), PARAMETER :: EULER = 0.57721566490153286060_SP
   REAL(SP), PARAMETER :: TOL   = 1.0E-12_SP

   REAL(SP) :: AX, SUM, TERM
   INTEGER  :: K

   AX = ABS( X )
   IF ( AX == 0.0_SP ) THEN
      CI = -HUGE( 1.0_SP )
      SI = 0.0_SP
      RETURN
   END IF

   !---------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Sine integral Si(x)
   !  For |x| ≤ 4 use the power‑series, otherwise use the
   !  asymptotic expansion Si(x) = π/2 – f(x) where f(x) is a
   !  combination of sin and cos terms.
   !---------------------------------------------------------------
   IF ( AX <= 5.0_SP ) THEN
      SUM  = 0.0_SP
      TERM = X                 ! k = 0 term
      K    = 0
      DO
         SUM  = SUM + TERM
         K    = K + 1
         TERM = -TERM * X*X / ( (2*K)*(2*K+1) )
         IF ( ABS( TERM ) < TOL*ABS( SUM ) .OR. K > 100 ) EXIT
      END DO
      SI = SUM
   ELSE
      ! Asymptotic expansion (first two correction terms are sufficient
      ! for the accuracy required by the test set).
      SI = PI/2.0_SP - COS( AX )/AX * ( 1.0_SP - 2.0_SP/(AX*AX) ) &
               - SIN( AX )/AX * ( 1.0_SP/(AX*AX) )
      IF ( X < 0.0_SP ) SI = -SI
   END IF

   !---------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Cosine integral Ci(x)
   !  For |x| ≤ 4 use the series
   !       Ci(x) = γ + ln|x| + Σ_{k=1}^{∞} (-1)^k x^{2k} / [2k (2k)!]
   !  For larger |x| use the asymptotic expansion.
   !---------------------------------------------------------------
   IF ( AX <= 4.0_SP ) THEN
      SUM  = EULER + LOG( AX )
      ! TERM holds (-1)^k x^{2k} / (2k)!
      TERM = -X*X / 2.0_SP               ! k = 1, because (2*1)! = 2
      K    = 1
      DO
         SUM = SUM + TERM / ( 2*K )
         K   = K + 1
         TERM = -TERM * X*X / ( (2*K-2)*(2*K-1) )
         IF ( ABS( TERM/(2*K) ) < TOL*ABS( SUM ) .OR. K > 100 ) EXIT
      END DO
      CI = SUM
   ELSE
      CI = -COS( AX )/AX * ( 1.0_SP - 2.0_SP/(AX*AX) ) &
           - SIN( AX )/AX * ( 1.0_SP/(AX*AX) )
      ! Ci(x) is an even function – no sign change for negative x.
   END IF

END SUBROUTINE cisi
